newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling stable vs dlr, drop likely.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling stable vs dlr, drop likely.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling held steady against the dollar on Friday in a matched market and the central bank governor hinted at marginal losses in coming days.
"We are conscious of the fact that the recent trends in the shilling exchange rate may be hurting exporters," Governor Micah Cheserem said in a speech at a horticulture exhibition.

"We at the central bank would therefore have no objection to a progressive movement in the shilling exchange rate to levels acceptable to both importers and exporters as long as the movement is in response to economic fundamentals," he added.
Cheserem emphasised that any action taken by the central bank to align the shilling exchange rate or ease the high level of interest rates should not generate inflationary pressures.
He said central bank policy was to let the shilling exchange rate be determined by market forces of demand and supply.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 54.93 unchanged for the fourth day, while against the pound it was posted at a mean rate of 87.55 from 87.84 on Thursday.
"A lot of the supply received from regular corporates was matched by demand from foreign investors who were in the market to buy treasury bills," a dealer told Reuters.
Dealers said with little incentive to trade, the shilling was set to remain stable in the short run.
Dealers have previously said the central bank was buying dollars to stem a shilling rise.
The money market was liquid with overnight rates quoted below 10 percent compared to 8-13 percent on Thursday.
